launch_app.description: Launch an app by its catalogue triple. The TV does not enumerate apps, so the values come from a client-side catalogue (smartcast_common.apps); NAME_SPACES 2 and 4 are interchangeable, and MESSAGE is null for most apps.

app_id.description: Catalogue APP_ID, e.g. "4" for Prime Video.

message.description: Optional launch message (usually null; some cast-backed apps need a JSON payload here).

name_space.description: Catalogue NAME_SPACE; 2 and 4 are treated as equivalent by clients.

press_channel_prev.description: Jump to the previously watched channel.

press_digit_0.description: Channel digit 0 (ASCII codeset; rejected on tuner-less models).

press_home.description: Home key (codeset 4, code 15 as pyvizio maps it).

press_info.description: Show info for the current channel or input.

press_mute_off.description: Mute off (may only work as a toggle on some sets).

press_mute_on.description: Mute on (may only work as a toggle on some sets).

press_mute_toggle.description: Mute toggle. The discrete on/off pairs below exist but openHAB notes some sets only honour the toggle.

press_power_on.description: Power the TV on — reliable only from a warm power mode; see smartcast_common.power.

set_input.description: Switch to a named input. VALUE comes from the Input List read; HASHVAL must be the CURRENT input's hash from a fresh Current Input read — the read-back is part of the send (smartcast_common.settings_tree).

hashval.description: Optimistic-concurrency token; read it from Current Input immediately before writing.

input_name.description: An ITEMS[x].NAME from the Input List read, e.g. "HDMI-1".

match.description: DIAL is answered by every DIAL-capable TV on the LAN (Roku, Fire TV, ...), so the target alone does not identify a Vizio. Fetch the LOCATION description document and keep only respondents whose device/manufacturer is exactly "VIZIO" — the filter pyvizio applies.

tls.notes: The TV's API port speaks HTTPS with a self-signed certificate; pin the leaf on first contact rather than validating a chain that ends nowhere.

device.name: Vizio SmartCast TV
device.notes: Vizio SmartCast TVs (2016 and later) expose a local HTTPS API on port 7345 (firmware 4.0 and newer; pre-4.0 firmware serves the same API on port 9000). Both ports speak HTTPS only and will not answer plain HTTP; the certificate is self-signed (CN historically BG2.prod.vizio.com), so clients must skip chain verification. Control requires pairing first: PUT /pairing/start makes the TV show a 4-digit PIN, PUT /pairing/pair trades the PIN for an AUTH_TOKEN, and every authenticated request then carries it in an AUTH header. Key events go to PUT /key_command/ as (CODESET, CODE, ACTION) triples, apps launch through PUT /app/launch, inputs and every on-screen setting live under /menu_native/, and GET /state/device/power_mode is the power reading. Sound bars (SmartCast "speakers") share the API shape with audio_settings in place of tv_settings and usually need no auth token; this spec covers the TV class. The API server stops when the set sleeps, so wake needs a WoL magic packet and does not work with the set in Eco power mode.

openness.notes: Vizio publishes nothing about this API; everything here is community reconstruction, exercised daily by pyvizio/vizaio (Home Assistant's backend) and the openHAB binding. No part of this spec has been replayed against hardware by this project, so every command is verification "reported".

issued_to_client: AUTH_TOKEN (sent as the AUTH header on every authenticated request)
credentials.notes: The token is a bearer credential with no documented expiry or rotation; any host holding it can drive the TV from the LAN. Identity reads (/state/device/deviceinfo, serial_number, version, ESN) answer WITHOUT a token — by design, since pyvizio reads the serial before pairing — so they must not be treated as secret material.
stored_on_device: Paired client list with issued AUTH tokens

factory_reset.effect: Clears settings, network credentials, paired mobile devices (and therefore every issued AUTH token) and tuned channels; the set returns to first-run setup. Documented by Vizio support and secondary write-ups, not replayed here.

steps.action: Settings > System > Reset & Admin > Reset TV to Factory Defaults (older firmware: Admin & Privacy).
Enter the administrative passcode (default 0000) and confirm Reset.
steps.expect: The set resets and power-cycles into first-run setup.

methods.description: First-run setup happens on the TV itself: language, network, terms, firmware update. Once the set is on the LAN, the client pairs for control. Pair with the TV already ON — pyvizio's README notes the set can "forget" the PIN if it was off when pairing started.

steps.action: Complete the on-screen first-run setup (network, terms) with the remote.
steps.expect: TV is online and answers SSDP/DIAL discovery.

steps.action: Open pairing; the TV shows a 4-digit PIN at the top of the screen.
steps.expect: JSON response ITEM carries PAIRING_REQ_TOKEN and CHALLENGE_TYPE.

steps.action: Read the PIN from the TV screen and hand it to the client.
Submit the PIN to finish pairing.
steps.expect: STATUS.RESULT == "success" and ITEM.AUTH_TOKEN present; store the token. PAIRING_DENIED means the PIN was wrong, MAX_CHALLENGES_EXCEEDED means too many failed tries (restart from /pairing/start), BLOCKED means another pairing is already in progress.

steps.action: Confirm control with the stored token.
steps.expect: STATUS.RESULT == "success" with the AUTH header set.

setup.notes: Two separate things happen here and neither needs the vendor cloud: network onboarding, done on the TV's own screen, and client pairing, which is the API-level step that issues the AUTH token. Pairing is per-client: each new client runs it once and stores the token, and the token survives until the user deletes the client under Settings > System > Mobile Devices (or factory-resets the set). Confidence is medium: the flow is documented by the exiva write-up and exercised by pyvizio/openHAB, but this project has not run it against hardware.

rejoin.notes: Moving networks is a device-UI operation (Settings > Network); a factory reset is never needed just to change routers, and issued AUTH tokens survive a network change.

entities.name: Power
entities.notes: ITEMS[0].VALUE: 1 = on, 0 = standby. Authenticated, and unreachable rather than wrong while the set is fully asleep (smartcast_common.power) — read unreachable as not-confirmed-on, never as a reason to skip the discrete off. turn_on is reliable only from a warm power mode.

entities.name: Power Key
entities.notes: The raw remote key, distinct from the Power switch above: it promises a keypress, not a direction. Discrete on/off commands exist (press_power_on/off); the toggle is what the physical remote's one power key sends.

entities.name: Play
entities.notes: Play and pause are discrete keys here, not one toggle.

entities.name: Input Next
entities.notes: Cycles inputs; direct selection is the Input select below.

entities.name: Input
entities.notes: Options: GET Input List — every ITEMS[x].NAME is one option ("HDMI-1", "COMP", ...). Current value: GET Current Input — ITEMS[0].VALUE; "SMARTCAST"/"CAST" mean an app is foreground and no listed input is current. Selecting sends set_input, whose HASHVAL must come from a fresh Current Input read.

entities.name: Power Mode
entities.notes: ITEMS[0].VALUE: 1 = on, 0 = standby. Unreachable while fully asleep.

entities.name: Current Input
entities.notes: ITEMS[0].VALUE is the input name; SMARTCAST/CAST while an app runs.

entities.name: Current App
entities.notes: ITEM.VALUE is {APP_ID, NAME_SPACE, MESSAGE}; empty VALUE means no app running. Mapping to a name needs the external app catalogue.

http_endpoints.description: Unauthenticated. Opens a pairing session; the TV displays a 4-digit PIN. Save DEVICE_ID (needed again to finish or cancel) and the returned PAIRING_REQ_TOKEN and CHALLENGE_TYPE. Results include BLOCKED (pairing already in progress) and MAX_CHALLENGES_EXCEEDED.
http_endpoints.name: Begin Pairing

fields.description: Name the TV lists under Settings > System > Mobile Devices.
fields.name: DEVICE_NAME

http_endpoints.description: Unauthenticated. Trades the on-screen PIN for the AUTH_TOKEN the client must store and send as the AUTH header thereafter. RESPONSE_VALUE is the PIN as a string; PAIRING_REQ_TOKEN and CHALLENGE_TYPE are from Begin Pairing. Results include PAIRING_DENIED (wrong PIN) and VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE.
http_endpoints.name: Finish Pairing

fields.description: The 4-digit PIN shown on the TV.
fields.name: RESPONSE_VALUE

http_endpoints.description: Unauthenticated. Aborts an in-progress pairing; per the exiva write-up RESPONSE_VALUE is hard-coded "1111" for cancellation.
http_endpoints.name: Cancel Pairing

http_endpoints.description: Unauthenticated (pyvizio reads it before pairing). Device info document; the model name sits at ITEMS[0].VALUE.system_info.model_name on TVs (plain VALUE.name on sound bars). This is the on-device identity read after SSDP has found the host.
http_endpoints.name: Device Info

http_endpoints.description: Unauthenticated (pyvizio uses it as the pre-pairing unique id). ITEMS[0].VALUE is the serial string — the spec's primary stable identity key. Newer firmware moved the system_information branch under admin_and_privacy; pyvizio carries both spellings and tries the alternate on failure.
http_endpoints.name: Serial Number

http_endpoints.description: Unauthenticated. ITEMS[0].VALUE is the firmware version string.
http_endpoints.name: Firmware Version

http_endpoints.description: Authenticated. ITEMS[0].VALUE is 1 (on) or 0 (standby). Unreachable rather than wrong when the set is fully asleep — see smartcast_common.power.
http_endpoints.name: Power Mode

http_endpoints.description: Authenticated. Sends remote key events; see smartcast_common.key_commands for the codeset table and hold semantics. Trailing slash is part of the path as documented and as pyvizio sends it.
http_endpoints.name: Key Command

fields.description: List of {CODESET: int, CODE: int, ACTION: KEYPRESS|KEYDOWN|KEYUP}; multiple entries chain into one request.
fields.name: KEYLIST

http_endpoints.description: Authenticated. ITEM.VALUE is {APP_ID, NAME_SPACE, MESSAGE} for the foreground app, or empty when none is running; NAME_SPACE 0 means a cast session. Mapping the pair to a name needs the external app catalogue — see smartcast_common.apps.
http_endpoints.name: Current App

http_endpoints.description: Authenticated. Launches an app by its catalogue triple. There is no on-device app list to enumerate first — see smartcast_common.apps.
http_endpoints.name: Launch App

http_endpoints.description: Authenticated. ITEMS holds one item per physical/logical input; ITEMS[x].NAME ("HDMI-1", "COMP", "TV", ...) is the VALUE a switch sends, and VALUE.NAME/METADATA describe it. SMARTCAST is not an entry here — it reads through Current Input while an app runs.
http_endpoints.name: Input List

http_endpoints.description: Authenticated. ITEMS[0].VALUE is the active input name ("SMARTCAST" or "CAST" while an app is foreground) and ITEMS[0].HASHVAL is the concurrency token a switch must echo back.
http_endpoints.name: Current Input

http_endpoints.description: Authenticated. Switches the input: VALUE is a NAME from Input List, HASHVAL is the CURRENT INPUT's hash from a fresh read (not the list's). Read-modify-write, per smartcast_common.settings_tree.
http_endpoints.name: Set Input

http_endpoints.description: Authenticated. Reads one settings group (picture, audio, timers, network, channels, closed_captions, devices, system, mobile_devices, cast, and their sub-paths). ITEMS carry CNAME/NAME/TYPE/VALUE/ HASHVAL; /menu_native/static/tv_settings/{cname} gives the allowed choices. See smartcast_common.settings_tree.
http_endpoints.name: Settings Read

http_endpoints.description: Authenticated. Writes one setting with {"REQUEST": "MODIFY", "HASHVAL": <from the read>, "VALUE": <typed per the item's TYPE>}. exiva warns an invalid VALUE can brick sets — honour the static options table and TYPE.
http_endpoints.name: Settings Write

apps.description: PUT /app/launch with {"VALUE": {"APP_ID": str, "NAME_SPACE": int, "MESSAGE": str|null}} launches an app; GET /app/current returns the foreground one as ITEM.VALUE with the same three fields, or an empty VALUE when none is running (pyvizio reports that as _NO_APP_RUNNING, and an unrecognised (APP_ID, NAME_SPACE) pair as _UNKNOWN_APP). NAME_SPACES 2 and 4 are treated as equivalent by pyvizio, and NAME_SPACE 0 means a cast session. THE TV DOES NOT LIST ITS APPS: the (APP_ID, NAME_SPACE, MESSAGE) catalogue comes from Vizio's app-catalog service or a client's bundled copy (pyvizio ships one in pyvizio/data/apps.json), so an app launcher is a static-table select, not a device-backed one. SmartCast Home itself is launchable as APP_ID "1", NAME_SPACE 4. While an app is in the foreground the current_input reads "SMARTCAST" or "CAST".

key_commands.description: Remote keys are PUT /key_command/ with {"KEYLIST": [{"CODESET": int, "CODE": int, "ACTION": "KEYPRESS"|"KEYDOWN"|"KEYUP"}]}. KEYPRESS is press-and-release; KEYDOWN/KEYUP pair for a hold. The KEYLIST array can string several key events into one request. Codesets are families: 0 ASCII (channel digits 0-9 are codes 48-57), 2 transport, 3 D-pad, 4 navigation, 5 audio, 6 video, 7 input, 8 channel, 9 color/exit, 11 power. The full (codeset, code) table this spec implements lives in the `commands` block below; pyvizio const.py is the source of record. Home Assistant additionally documents a `guide` command whose codeset/code pair does not appear in pyvizio or the exiva tables — not catalogued here for lack of a sourced value.

power.description: GET /state/device/power_mode answers ITEMS[0].VALUE as 1 (on) or 0 (standby). The API server itself is down while the set sleeps, so a powered-off TV is unreachable rather than answering 0 forever; waking it needs a Wake-on-LAN magic packet, which does not work when the set's Settings > System > Power Mode is Eco Mode (the "Quickstart"/moderate modes keep the network stack warm enough). POW_ON (11,1) is therefore only reliable from the warm-standby modes.

request_format.description: Requests go to https://<ip>:<port><path> with <port> 7345 on firmware 4.0+ and 9000 on older sets (try 7345 first, fall back). Bodies are JSON; every PUT sets Content-Type: application/json. Authenticated requests add one header, spelled AUTH by pyvizio (HTTP header names are case-insensitive; exiva writes it Auth): AUTH: <AUTH_TOKEN>. The pairing endpoints themselves are unauthenticated, as are the identity reads.
request_format.escaping: JSON strings, nothing further. Setting values that are strings in the UI ("On", "HDMI-1") are sent as JSON strings; sliders take integers; the wire type to send is stated by the item's TYPE field in the settings read.

http.body: JSON object per endpoint; GETs send none.
http.headers: Content-Type: application/json on PUTs; AUTH: <token> on authenticated calls.

response_format.description: Every response is a JSON object with a STATUS envelope {"RESULT": ..., "DETAIL": ...}, the requested URI, and a TIME string. HTTP status codes are NOT meaningful — the API answers 200 for failures and the verdict lives in STATUS.RESULT ("success", "failure", "uri_not_found", "requires_pairing", "invalid_parameter", ...). A client that checks only the HTTP status will report failed writes as delivered. Query endpoints answer ITEMS (a list of items with CNAME/NAME/TYPE/VALUE/HASHVAL); pairing answers a single ITEM.

settings_tree.description: All on-screen settings are a readable/writable tree under /menu_native/dynamic/tv_settings/<cname> (audio_settings on sound bars); /menu_native/static/tv_settings/<cname> enumerates the allowed choices/ranges. Reads return ITEMS with TYPE telling the value kind (T_VALUE_V1 on/off-style, T_VALUE_ABS_V1 slider, T_LIST_V1 choice, T_MENU_V1 submenu, ...). WRITES ARE READ-MODIFY-WRITE: PUT /menu_native/dynamic/tv_settings/<cname>/ <item_cname> with {"REQUEST": "MODIFY", "VALUE": ..., "HASHVAL": <current hash from the read>} — the HASHVAL is optimistic concurrency, and a stale one is rejected. exiva warns that writing an out-of-range value can brick sets; honour the static options and the TYPE. Top-level CNAME groups include picture, audio, timers, network, channels, closed_captions, devices, system, mobile_devices, cast. Inputs are the devices subtree: devices/name_input lists inputs (ITEMS[x].NAME is the switchable name), devices/current_input reads/switches the active one, and the current input's own HASHVAL (not the list's) is what a switch sends back.

tls.description: HTTPS only, on both ports; plain HTTP gets no answer. The TV serves a self-signed certificate (CN observed historically as BG2.prod.vizio.com); clients must disable chain and hostname verification, exactly as pyvizio does with ssl=False.

smartcast_common.transport_gap: The reference app today implements HTTP GET/POST with an empty body and no custom headers. This protocol needs FOUR things it does not have: (1) HTTPS with certificate verification disabled (self-signed TV certificate), (2) PUT requests with a JSON body and Content-Type: application/json, (3) an AUTH header on every request after pairing, (4) for settings writes, a read-modify-write carrying the current HASHVAL back. Every `commands` entry below therefore states the real method and arguments but is NOT sendable by the reference app as-is; a consumer must implement the transport described here first. The unauthenticated GETs (Device Info, Serial Number, Version, ESN) are the exception — only the TLS step gates them.
